status_effects.explanation: The duchess's expressed affection and lasting grief for Saint-Loup locally elevate his image, in contrast to her harsh treatment of Gilberte in the same speech.

Gilberte's friendly initiative to introduce her daughter draws the narrator warmly into her family circle and gives him explicit pleasure, a modest gain in social/emotional standing as a participant in the scene.
Her transformation from bourgeois salon hostess into princesse de Guermantes is noted as a notable rise in rank, though the narrator's tone carries mild irony about this trajectory.

appraisal_events.evidence: ça me faisait beaucoup de peine à cause du pauvre Saint-Loup... j'aimais bien le pauvre Saint-Loup... il m'arrive encore de penser à lui. Je n'oublie personne.
appraisal_events.explanation: In the midst of condemning Gilberte, the duchess separately voices enduring affection, grief, and continued memory of Saint-Loup, sympathetically elevating him even as she reframes his death as near self-sacrifice from family sorrow.

appraisal_events.evidence: Si vous le permettez, je vais aller chercher ma fille pour vous la présenter... Je suis sûre qu'elle sera une gentille amie pour vous.
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte warmly offers to bring her daughter to meet the narrator, an inclusive gesture that the narrator himself marks with explicit pleasure and astonishment, staging him as favored participant rather than mere observer.

appraisal_events.evidence: ma présentation à Mlle de Saint-Loup allait avoir lieu chez Mme Verdurin devenue princesse de Guermantes !
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator marks with an exclamation the remarkable social ascent of the former salon hostess into the title of princesse de Guermantes, a rise the novel elsewhere treats with characteristic irony toward Mme Verdurin's social climbing.
